dedupe_keys.name: physics based pedestrian modeling physped data driven langevin pedestrian model

description: physics-based-pedestrian-modeling is a Python package that builds physics-based pedestrian models from trajectory measurements, implementing the data-driven generalised Langevin model of Pouw, van der Vleuten, Corbetta and Toschi at Eindhoven University of Technology, published in Physical Review E in December 2024. The model captures both the deterministic movement and the stochastic fluctuations of walking and is meant to work in any environment where extensive trajectory data exist. The package ships with documentation, a Colab quick-start notebook and test and coverage reports, and it is built to process the authors' Eindhoven Centraal platform trajectory dataset. Coverage: generic; the worked example is a railway station platform in the Netherlands. Access: install from PyPI (version 0.3.8 of 2025-06-17, Python 3.11 or later) or from the repository. Licence: BSD 3-Clause; free. Caveats: the model needs large trajectory datasets for fitting and describes normal walking, not emergency evacuation. Simulation uses are realistic pedestrian motion in stations and public spaces for crowd and capacity studies, and as a data-driven check on agent-based evacuation models. Related records: the Eindhoven Centraal platform trajectory dataset and the MassMotion and Pathfinder records.
